title: Best Immersion Blenders 2026: Soup, Smoothie & More
summary: Lumpy soup, splattered walls, a pot you have to pour into a blender. A good immersion blender ends all of that for a fraction of a countertop blender's price. We narrowed 2026's best to 6, from the Breville Control Grip to a budget Hamilton Beach.
method: We combined recommendations from Good Housekeeping, Bon Appétit and RTINGS, which each test many hand blenders. A pick ranked higher when more than one of them praised it, then we sorted the winners by use: soup, attachments, cordless, smoothies and budget.
assumptions: Prices change often, so check Amazon for today's price. Hand blenders are great for soups and sauces but cannot crush ice like a countertop blender.

products.name: Breville Control Grip Immersion Blender
why: The pick for people who want one hand blender to do it all: 15 speeds, an anti-suction base and a whisk, jug and food-processing bowl in the box.
It is great at soups, so it ends the pour-the-pot-into-a-blender mess.
specs: Whisk, blending jug and food-processing bowl included
pros: Handles soups, sauces and light prep
Less splatter than most stick blenders
cons: Takes more storage space with all attachments
products.best_for: Home cooks who want one tool for soups, sauces and light chopping
products.skip_if: You only need a basic blender for the occasional smoothie

products.name: Braun MultiQuick 7 3-in-1 Immersion Blender
why: The choice for cooks who want attachments: a beaker, whisk and chopper, plus easy speed control for sauces, soups and baby food.
Braun has led this category for years, and this is its most versatile model.
specs: 3-in-1 set with beaker, whisk and chopper
cons: Costs more than basic hand blenders
Fails to crush ice well, like most stick blenders
products.best_for: Cooks who want attachments to chop, whisk and puree
products.skip_if: You want the cheapest possible hand blender

products.name: Vitamix Immersion Blender
why: Good Housekeeping lists the Vitamix Immersion as the best for soup due to its power and versatility.
Food Network reviews the Vitamix Explorian (full‑size) but confirms Vitamix’s reputation for robust performance.
cons: Costs more than basic stick blenders
products.best_for: Those who frequently make soups and need a reliable, powerful immersion blender
products.skip_if: You only need a lightweight, budget option

products.name: KitchenAid Go Cordless Hand Blender
why: RTINGS picked it as its cord-free choice, so you can blend at the stove or in a big pot without hunting for an outlet.
The battery platform works with other KitchenAid Go tools, which suits people who already own them.
pros: No cord to tangle or reach
Easy to move around the kitchen
Good for everyday soups and sauces
cons: Battery sold separately in some bundles
Less sustained power than corded models
products.best_for: Cooks who hate cords and already use cordless tools
products.skip_if: You want constant power for big batches

products.name: KitchenAid Two‑Speed Hand Blender
why: Good Housekeeping names the KitchenAid Two‑Speed Hand Blender the best for smoothies, citing its efficient blending of single‑serving drinks.
Consumer Reports lists KitchenAid among its tested brands.
cons: Fewer speed steps than premium models
Not ideal for heavy, thick blending
products.best_for: Smoothie lovers who want a quick, single‑serve solution
products.skip_if: You need high‑speed or heavy‑task blending

products.name: Hamilton Beach Two‑Speed Hand Blender
why: Good Housekeeping lists the Hamilton Beach Two‑Speed Hand Blender as the best value, balancing performance and affordability.
Consumer Reports includes Hamilton Beach in its brand list.
products.best_for: Budget‑conscious buyers who need a reliable hand blender
products.skip_if: You require advanced features or high power

intro: The best time to buy a hand blender is before you ruin another soup. They cost far less than a countertop blender, go straight into the pot and wash in seconds.
Black Friday is Nov 27, and small appliances like these are often discounted then. We re-check Amazon prices daily, so the card shows today's price.

voices.name: Breville Control Grip
voices.like: Rated fantastic for soups and great for professional use, plus it comes with a food-processing bowl and a whisk.
voices.catch: Only mediocre at crushing ice, though it still beats the Braun MultiQuick 5, which fails at it completely.

tips.title: Before you buy a hand blender
items: Hand blenders are for soup, sauces and light prep. None of the picks here crushes ice well, so for frozen drinks buy a countertop blender.
The long arm of the Breville reaches into a deep stockpot. A compact one is easier to store.
A cordless model like the KitchenAid Go moves freely but has less sustained power for big batches.
Tilt the blender so the blade never scrapes the bottom, and use the blade guard that comes with most models on coated or delicate pans.

faq: What is the best immersion blender?
The Breville Control Grip is our overall pick. The Braun MultiQuick 7 is the best if you want the most attachments.
Can an immersion blender crush ice?
Most cannot do it well. RTINGS rates even the Breville only mediocre at crushing ice.
Cordless is easier to move around the kitchen, corded gives steady power for large batches of soup.
Hand blender for soups, sauces and quick cleanup. Countertop blender for smoothies, ice and big batches.
